author: Karl Rock
description:
It is incredible to think that the concept of indoor plumbing is not a modern invention. Thousands of years ago, civilizations relied on terracotta pipes to manage water and waste just as effectively as the plastic systems we install in our homes today.

This particular drainage pipe stands as a testament to ancient engineering prowess of the Indus Valley Civilisation at Mohenjo-daro in Pakistan. Seeing a structure that has survived five millennia still embedded in the ground is a humbling reminder of human ingenuity.

The pipe was actually fully intact until it was destroyed during the massive 2022 floods in Sindh.

Archaeologists often find these systems across ancient sites, proving that complex sanitation and urban planning were priorities long before our time. It is fascinating to see how these fired clay sections were joined together, creating networks that allowed cities to function and thrive.
title: 5,000 Year Old Plumbing Secrets

author: Karl Rock
description:
Ancient engineering is always surprising, but this takes the prize for the most unexpected discovery. Archaeologists in Mohenjo-daro, Pakistan, found these public washrooms from thousands of years ago, featuring eight stalls and even double storey designs.

The genius is in the layout. Each door was built with an L shape to ensure total privacy. Even five millennia ago, people understood that using the bathroom should be a personal experience, even when everyone else is right next to you.

It serves as a reminder that some human needs and preferences for privacy really haven't changed much at all.
title: This Toilet is 5,000-Years-Old!
